From: Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@medixahealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-01T13:02:00Z
Subject: Tenant operator minimization & HSM rotation schedule — Privacy annex draft

Laura,

Thanks for sending the draft privacy annex. We had a chance to review it with our legal and security teams and have a few focused asks before we can route this for signature: 

1) Operator access scope: We need an explicit statement that operator access is limited to non-plaintext infrastructure telemetry and never to customer plaintext model inputs/outputs. If temporary access to decrypted data is required (e.g., for breakglass forensic), we need a tight process and notification window.

2) Key custody & rotation: Your draft mentions customer-controlled keys but we need the rotation schedule and the mechanism (HSM-based, KMS policy, split custody?). Please state the rotation frequency and whether Redwood holds any escrow of key material.

3) Subprocessor list & minimality: Please confirm which subprocessors will have any level of control-plane or ops access (including patching vendors). We prefer to limit subprocessors to named vendors and have a 30-day notice for additions.

4) Cross-border telemetry and logs: We need confirmation that operator-facing telemetry and control-plane logs containing tenant identifiers will be stored in US regions only (us-east-1 or us-west-2) unless otherwise consented.

Attached is a marked-up version of the annex pull. Can you and your security/ops leads respond inline and recommend language we can sign off on?

Regards,
Dana Ortiz
Head of Privacy
Medixa Health

Attachment: medixa_privacy_markups.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@medixahealth.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@medixahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-01T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Tenant operator minimization & HSM rotation schedule — Privacy annex draft

Dana / Carlos —

Thanks for the clear markup. Summary responses below and I'm attaching the updated annex, a network segmentation diagram, and a short change log for the DPA. High level: we can meet your asks with precise clauses and an operational playbook we will keep under limited distribution.

1) Operator access scope
- Clause proposed: "Operator access is restricted to control-plane actions that do not expose plaintext customer data. Under no circumstances will Redwood personnel access unencrypted customer model inputs or outputs except under documented breakglass procedures."
- Breakglass: we propose a documented ticketing + two-person authorization flow with automated tenant notification within 1 hour of any access. All sessions are recorded and retained as audit evidence.

2) Key custody & rotation
- Mode: Customer-managed keys in customer HSM (BYOK) or customer-managed KMS in customer VPC. Redwood will not retain private key material in escrow absent explicit, written agreement.
- Rotation: We propose a default rotation cadence of 90 days for ephemeral HSM session keys; root/master key rotation remains customer-managed. We can add optional automation scripts for rotation and automated rotation proofs (signed key attestations).

3) Subprocessors
- Current subprocessors limited to: OpsPatch Inc. (patching), VaultTransit Ltd. (secret delivery), and Redwood-managed monitoring (internal). We will provide a 30-day notice for additions and allow for objections from your security team per the DPA.

4) Cross-border telemetry/logs
- By default, operator-facing telemetry that includes tenant identifiers will be stored in US regions only (us-east-1). We can support EU-only retention options for an additional region restriction.

Attachments: privacy_annex_draft_v2.pdf (with inline redlines), network_segmentation_v3.png, dpa_change_log.xlsx

Next steps: please review the redlines. If acceptable we will generate a DocuSign packet for the DPA + annex and include a short ops playbook as an annex (access only after countersignature).

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Enterprise Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Tenant operator minimization & HSM rotation schedule — Privacy annex draft

Laura / Neha —

Quick tech confirmation and suggested clause wording for the annex.

- HSM and rotation: We will support BYOK with customer HSMs (PKCS#11) and provide an automated rotation helper that performs ephemeral session key generation every 90 days by default. Redwood will not hold any escrow copies of private key material unless Medixa requests a sealed escrow (we can document that as an optional addendum).

- Operator sessions: All operator sessions are ephemeral, initiated only through a jump-host tied to an ephemeral cert (30-minute TTL) and MFA. We log session start/stop, command transcripts, and typed commands; transcripts are encrypted at rest and access-controlled. Proposed wording: "Operator access is ephemeral, authenticated via short-lived certificates and multi-factor authentication, and session transcripts are retained for audit purposes only."

- Subprocessors: OpsPatch Inc. will have access for patch delivery but only via hashed package delivery (no remote RDP to tenant instances). Any vendor that requires direct access must be added to the subprocessor appendix and receives 30-day prior notice.

Marcus, can you confirm the retention windows we'll commit to in the annex? I propose 12 months for session transcripts (encrypted) and 24 months for control-plane audit logs; keen to hear if we need to tighten further for Medixa.

—Karthik
